text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the newest merged PR first. This gives us a clean baseline to measure its output against human reviews without disrupting active work. The trade-off is delayed feedback for open PRs, but we avoid noise from in-progress changes. Once we validate its performance on merged PRs, we’ll expand to open PRs to catch issues earlier.

name: Gauge
text: Shadow mode on merged PRs trains reviewers to ignore real issues because the feedback arrives too late—after the code is already in main. Instead, run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *open* PRs first; that catches problems before they’re committed, while still avoiding disruption. Settle it by comparing the volume and severity of issues flagged in open PRs versus merged ones over two weeks.

name: Overhaul
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *both* open and merged PRs from day one—this catches issues early without delaying feedback, and we can compare its output against human reviews immediately. The trade-off is higher initial effort, but it ensures we validate the tool’s performance across the full review cycle faster.

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on open PRs first. This catches review issues before they’re committed, which is the whole point of a review tool. The trade-off is we won’t see how it performs on merged PRs immediately, but we can add that later once we’ve tuned it on active work. Starting with open PRs keeps feedback timely and prevents the tool from being ignored because it’s “too late.”

name: Ratchet
text:
DECISION: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on open PRs first, then expand to merged PRs after one week of tuning.

Result: A validated baseline of PR-Agent’s output against human reviews on active work, with clear signal-to-noise metrics. Owner: Gauge.
